questions.q: Which layout is the most survivable on a single motor failure?
questions.explain: The coaxial partner and the opposite pair compensate both thrust and torque.

questions.q: What happens to a hexa with thrust margin (T/W ≥ 2 on the remaining five) on a motor failure?
options: An automatic landing on a timer
questions.explain: Five motors lift, but the CW/CCW balance is broken; with T/W < 2 it falls.

questions.q: Why are fuses not put on the motors?
options: It interferes with ESC telemetry and DShot
Pulsed current: it blows for nothing
questions.explain: Fuses go on the batteries, the BECs and the payload branches.

questions.q: How is the FC's BEC made redundant?
options: A backup from the USB connector
A large capacitor on the bus
questions.explain: If one fails, power keeps coming from the second.

questions.q: The current of an X8 arm relative to the motor current:
How do you simulate a motor failure in ArduPilot SITL?
questions.explain: SITL applies the multiplier to the output of the selected motors.

questions.q: What shows in the ArduPilot log on a motor failure?
options: The voltage rises and the battery current falls
questions.explain: One RCOU channel at maximum, its neighbor at minimum, RPM 0 in the ESC telemetry: the mixer is compensating.

questions.q: A flat octo compared with a hexa:
options: Needs less total thrust to hover the same mass
More margin, can survive two failures in lucky positions
questions.explain: Eight motors give more margin and, in a lucky arrangement, survive two failures.
